expectations.text: States upfront/early that this is text-based and real pronunciation/accent cannot be assessed
expectations.evidence: No caveat appears before or during the mock test (Parts 1-3 run straight through with only a one-line context note about the exam being in 2 weeks). The only mention of the text-based limitation is buried at the very end, inside the Pronunciation feedback section: '(Assessed from the phrasing, rhythm, and self-correction patterns visible in this transcript — in a real test this is judged on audio...)'. This is not upfront/early as the assertion requires.

expectations.text: Runs Part 1 with multiple short personal questions
expectations.evidence: 7 questions covering hometown, future plans, likes, work, free time, social preference, and food.

expectations.text: Runs Part 2 with a cue card (topic + bullet points) and some simulation of the 1-minute prep step (e.g. asking for prep notes/bullet points before the long-turn answer)
expectations.evidence: Gives a cue card with 4 bullet points and states 'you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say... You can make some notes if you wish. Do you have a pen and paper?' before the long-turn answer, though unlike the with_skill run it does not show the candidate's actual prep notes.

expectations.text: Runs Part 3 with questions that are progressively more abstract/discussion-based, tied to the Part 2 topic
expectations.evidence: 5 Part 3 questions move from personal factors in skill-learning to societal questions about technology and the future of education, all tied to the Part 2 'skill you'd like to learn' topic.

expectations.text: Gives final feedback broken down by the four official criteria (Fluency & Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range & Accuracy, Pronunciation) by name
expectations.evidence: Feedback has named sections for Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Pronunciation.

expectations.text: Gives an overall estimated band score
Does not claim to assess real pronunciation/accent from the text transcript (stays consistent with the upfront caveat)
expectations.evidence: Pronunciation section says stress/intonation/sound production 'cannot be fully verified here' and the band is based on 'typical correlates' rather than claiming a real listen.

claims.claim: The recurring present-continuous-for-present-perfect error ('I am working... since three years') is a systematic pattern worth prioritizing.
claims.evidence: The transcript does show this pattern recurring, so the grammar analysis itself is sound even though the upfront-caveat assertion fails.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — the missing upfront caveat is a genuine, meaningful gap (a student could run the whole test before learning its limits), and assertion 1 correctly catches it.
